correctness.rationale: A first color class either consists of a deleted matching nonedge pair (allowing an exact recursive peel of one crown index), or a full bipartition side, in which case exactly two colors are used. For t pair peels, predecessor constraints a_i<b_j and b_i<a_j for all 1<=i<=t<j describe an exact poset; different ordered pair-index choices yield disjoint permutations. Direct first-two/three vertex decomposition proves L(n,1)=(2n)!/n² and L(n,t)=3L(n−1,t−1); multiplied by n!/(n−t)! ordered choices yields the asserted tail distribution for all n≥2. Independent complete enumeration of all vertex permutations for n=2,3,4 matched counts (2:24), (2:480,3:240), and (2:30240,3:7200,4:2880), respectively. The source C++ verifier was inspected and checks all n≤5 and 28 poset cases through n9; our finite test is not used to prove the recurrence at arbitrary n.
